score_rationale: Exceptionally strong willingness-to-pay validated by active commercial market: at least 6 vendors (LakeB2B, Blue Mail Media, eSalesData, DataIncluder, BizInforUSA, ReadyContacts) currently selling CPA email lists ranging from 27,573 to 165,000+ records with pricing in the hundreds to thousands of dollars range. Four high-value B2B buyer segments: (1) banks and wealth management firms prospecting CPAs' high-net-worth clients, (2) CPE (Continuing Professional Education) providers marketing certification courses and training, (3) finance-focused staffing and recruiting firms, and (4) B2B software vendors (accounting software, tax prep, payroll, practice management). All 50 states plus DC maintain public CPA registries via their State Boards of Accountancy with downloadable or scrapable data including licensee name, license number, status (active/inactive), issue/renewal dates, firm affiliation, and city/state. Zero PII — all professional credential data. Engineering lift is moderate: scrape or download from 51 state board websites, deduplicate across multi-state license holders, normalize firm names, and enrich with practice area flags (tax, audit, forensic, etc.) where indicated. No affordable flat-file competitor exists on Gumroad or similar marketplaces — all existing vendors sell annual subscriptions ($500-$3,000/year) or per-record pricing, leaving a clear gap for a one-time $79-$99 CSV. Audience size is massive: AICPA reports 750,000+ active CPAs nationwide, creating a TAM of 10,000+ potential B2B buyers (software vendors, banks, training providers, recruiters). Score is 8 due to validated high willingness-to-pay from multiple commercial vendors, confirmed public data availability across all states, absence of low-cost flat-file alternatives, and clear B2B buyer segments with proven purchasing behavior.
summary: A cleaned CSV of all active Certified Public Accountant (CPA) licenses extracted from all 50 state Boards of Accountancy plus DC — fully public and downloadable/scrapable without authentication. Each record includes the CPA's full name, license number, license status (active, inactive, expired, revoked), initial issue date, current expiration/renewal date, firm name or affiliation (where listed), city and state of practice, and license type (CPA, PA in some states). As of 2026, approximately 750,000 CPAs hold active licenses nationwide (note: some CPAs hold multi-state licenses, so unique individual count is ~650,000). B2B software vendors (accounting software like QuickBooks, Xero, TaxDome; practice management platforms; CRM for accountants) pay $1,000-$3,000/year for CPA email lists to target with product demos and free trials. Banks and wealth management firms use CPA lists to identify tax professionals who serve high-net-worth clients for referral partnerships and joint marketing. CPE providers (courses, webinars, certifications for maintaining CPA license) spend heavily on CPA marketing lists to promote required continuing education. Finance staffing and recruiting firms pay $500-$2,000/year for CPA databases to source candidates for audit, tax, and advisory roles. A one-time $79-$99 CSV undercuts annual subscription vendors by 80%+ while targeting the same B2B buyer segments.

audience.who: B2B accounting software vendors (Intuit QuickBooks, Xero, FreshBooks, Zoho Books, Wave, TaxDome, Karbon, Jetpack Workflow) marketing practice management, tax prep, client portals, and workflow automation tools to CPA firms — CPAs represent a high-LTV segment ($500-$5,000/year per firm) and software vendors routinely pay $1,000-$3,000/year for targeted CPA email lists; CPE (Continuing Professional Education) course providers and certification platforms (Surgent CPE, Becker Professional Education, Wiley CPELink, CPA Academy) selling required continuing education to maintain CPA licensure — all CPAs must complete 40-120 hours of CPE every 1-3 years depending on state, creating a recurring $200-$1,000/year spend per CPA; finance and accounting staffing agencies and recruiting firms (Robert Half, Ajilon, Accountemps, KPMG Talent, plus thousands of boutique CPA recruiters) sourcing candidates for audit, tax, forensic accounting, and CFO roles — a single placement generates $15,000-$50,000 in recruiting fees, making a $79 database trivial; banks, wealth management firms, and insurance brokers (regional banks, Edward Jones, Fidelity, Northwestern Mutual) building referral partnerships with CPAs who serve high-net-worth clients — CPAs control access to business owners and affluent individuals, making them high-value referral sources for loans, investment management, and life insurance products; professional liability insurance carriers (Hiscox, The Hartford, CNA, CAMICO) underwriting E&O policies for CPA firms, where premiums range from $1,500-$15,000/year per firm.

data_wanted: All 50 state Boards of Accountancy plus DC maintain public CPA registries, accessible via state-specific websites under names like '[State] Board of Accountancy', '[State] Board of Public Accountancy', or '[State] Accountancy Board'. No authentication required for lookup (though some states may require scraping vs. bulk download). Key fields per license: CPA full name (first, middle initial, last), license number (format varies by state, typically 5-8 digits or alphanumeric), license status (active, inactive, lapsed, expired, suspended, revoked), original issue date, current expiration or renewal date, firm name or employer (where publicly listed — availability varies by state; sole practitioners may list 'Self-Employed' or DBA name), practice address city and state (some states list full street address, others only city/state), and license type (CPA is standard; some states also list PA 'Public Accountant' for legacy pre-CPA licenses). Target all active and inactive-but-not-revoked licenses (exclude only revoked, surrendered, or disciplinary-suspended). Scope to individual CPAs only — exclude CPA firms (which have separate firm registrations in many states). Approximately 750,000 active CPA licenses nationwide as of 2026 (note: multi-state license holders mean unique individual count is ~650,000-700,000). Target output: 750,000 rows, one per license. Data is 100% public per state accountancy statutes (professional licensing records are public information under state Freedom of Information laws).

willingness_to_pay.signal: Five distinct buyer segments with validated purchasing behavior and high LTV justification. (1) B2B accounting software vendors: platforms like QuickBooks, Xero, TaxDome, and practice management tools generate $500-$5,000/year per CPA firm in subscription revenue; these vendors routinely pay $1,000-$3,000/year for targeted CPA email lists (confirmed by LakeB2B, Blue Mail Media pricing models), making a $79 one-time CSV deliver 12×-38× savings vs. annual subscriptions. A single new software customer acquired yields 6×-60× ROI. (2) CPE providers: all CPAs must complete 40-120 hours of continuing education every 1-3 years (state-dependent) to maintain licensure, creating a mandatory recurring spend of $200-$1,000/year per CPA; CPE course vendors pay $500-$2,000/year for CPA marketing lists, so a $79 CSV provides 6×-25× cost savings. (3) Finance staffing and recruiting firms: a single CPA placement for audit, tax, or CFO roles generates $15,000-$50,000 in recruiter fees; a $79 database of 750K CPAs to source candidates is trivial against one successful placement (190×-630× ROI). (4) Banks and wealth management firms: CPAs serve as referral sources for high-net-worth clients (business owners, executives, investors); a single referred client generates $1,000-$10,000/year in wealth management fees or loan interest, making a $79 CPA referral partner list negligible. (5) Professional liability insurers: E&O policies for CPA firms range $1,500-$15,000/year; insurers targeting 1,000 CPA firms from a $79 list need only 5-10 new policies to break even. The absence of any flat-file competitor below $500 (all existing vendors sell annual subscriptions or per-record pricing, not one-time CSV downloads) creates a clear low-price entry wedge.
